answer: A cryptographic beacon paired with verifiable delay functions deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate sequential, non-parallelizable proofs during registration epochs. Rather than deploying an ocean of autonomous clones costlessly, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated sequential processor time per identity. A limitation is that when adversary ASIC efficiency nears its zenith, specialized hardware outpaces commodity nodes and centralizes identity issuance.
